subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
unit: Unit 5: A Letter to a Teacher (Writing)
lesson: Formal and informal language; drafting the letter / Checking and editing a partner’s letter; writing the second draft
outcomes: Tell formal and informal expressions apart
Write a formal letter to a new English teacher
Edit a partner's letter and write a second draft

tf.why: Yes, it is used in formal letters.

tf.s: 'Love from' is a good ending for a letter to a director.
tf.why: 'Love from' is informal; a director needs a formal ending.

tf.s: 'Dear…' can be used in both formal and informal letters.
tf.why: Right, 'Dear' works in both kinds of letter.

tf.s: 'I would be grateful if…' is formal language.
tf.why: Correct, it is a polite formal phrase.

tf.s: When you check a partner's letter, you look at meaning and content first.
tf.why: Yes, the ideas must be clear first.

tf.s: A second draft means writing a completely new letter.
tf.why: You only add the corrections and changes to your first draft.

tf.s: You must accept every comment your partner gives you.
tf.why: You decide which comments are useful and keep those.

tf.s: You underline ideas you don't understand in pencil.
tf.why: Yes, pencil marks are gentle and easy to remove.

tf.s: The final draft goes into the portfolio with the earlier drafts.
tf.why: Well done, the portfolio shows how your writing improved.

boxes.q: Which ending can close a formal letter with a friendly tone?
boxes.why: 'Best wishes' can be used in both kinds of letter.

boxes.q: Who is the letter in this unit written to?
boxes.why: You introduce yourself to a new English teacher.

boxes.q: What helps you check your partner's language?
boxes.why: The checklist has questions about language.

boxes.q: Why do we use formal language in this letter?
o: It is addressed to a teacher
It is to a close friend
An improved copy of the first draft
A letter on a new topic

boxes.q: What do you attach to your second draft?
boxes.why: The first draft shows your progress.

boxes.q: Which is a formal opening sentence?
o: I am writing to introduce myself to you.
boxes.why: This sentence is polite and formal.

boxes.q: Which paragraph comes first in the letter?
boxes.why: Every letter starts with an introduction.
Feedback helps you make your writing better.

hunt.q: A file that keeps all your drafts
A list of questions to check work
Check this first in a letter
A letter to a teacher uses…
The last paragraph of the letter

mcq.q: Which list shows the correct order of the letter's paragraphs?
o: Introduction, family, spare time, plans, learning English, conclusion
Conclusion, family, introduction, plans, spare time, learning English
Plans, introduction, conclusion, family, spare time, learning English
Family, conclusion, spare time, introduction, plans, learning English
mcq.why: The letter starts with an introduction and ends with a conclusion.

mcq.q: What do you check in a partner's letter?
mcq.why: The checklist covers meaning and language.

mcq.q: What should you do with the comments from your partner?
o: Decide which ones are useful and keep them
mcq.why: Not all advice is useful, so you choose.

o: Ending a formal letter with a friendly tone

mcq.q: You are writing to your new English teacher. Which ending is best?
mcq.why: A letter to a teacher needs a formal ending.

mcq.q: Your partner wrote: 'First I want to tell you about my family.' Which comment is useful?
o: You should add a comma after 'First'.
mcq.why: Helpful feedback is clear and specific.

mcq.q: Which sentence suits a formal letter?
o: I would be grateful if you could help me with my writing.
Hi there! Help me with writing, OK?
mcq.why: Formal letters use polite, complete sentences.

mcq.q: Why is 'Love from' not suitable for a letter to a teacher?
o: It is informal and too personal
It is a greeting, not an ending
mcq.why: Teachers get formal endings like 'Yours faithfully'.

mcq.q: Why don't you write a whole new letter for the second draft?
o: You only need to add the corrections and changes
The first draft is always perfect
mcq.why: A second draft improves the first one.

mcq.q: Why do you check the meaning of a letter before small language errors?
o: A letter must first make sense to the reader
Meaning is easier to fix at the end
mcq.why: Clear ideas come first, then accuracy.
